businessModel.summary: Rolls-Royce designs and manufactures engines and power systems across three divisions: Civil Aerospace (large engines for wide-body aircraft, with revenue from both engine sales and long-term "TotalCare" maintenance service contracts billed per flying hour), Defence (military aero-engines and systems), and Power Systems (engines/generators for marine, data centre backup, and industrial use).
businessModel.source: Rolls-Royce Holdings plc Annual Report — business overview (https://www.rolls-royce.com/investors.aspx)

competitiveMoat.summary: Wide-body jet engines are a duopoly/triopoly market (Rolls-Royce, GE/CFM, Pratt & Whitney) with very high certification and switching costs; long-life service contracts (installed base of engines already flying) create decades of recurring aftermarket revenue, though programme execution and input cost risk can hurt margins.
competitiveMoat.source: Rolls-Royce Annual Report / public analyst commentary — verify against the latest filing

bullCase.researchNote: Fallback only — the app auto-generates bull-case bullets from live financial/analyst data when enough is available (see backend/src/lib/deriveBullBear.js). Note Finnhub's free tier has thin coverage for the Rolls-Royce US ADR (RYCEY) used as a stand-in for the LSE listing, so this fallback is more likely to be needed for RR.L than for NVDA. If you want a richer case, add your own 2-4 points (e.g. turnaround progress, widebody flying hours recovery, defence demand), with your own source(s) and date.

bearCase.researchNote: Fallback only — same as bullCase above. If you want a richer case, add your own 2-4 points on the key risks (e.g. execution risk, input costs, aerospace cycle), with your own source(s) and date.

analystConsensus.researchNote: Fallback only — the app pulls a real analyst consensus rating live from Finnhub (via the RYCEY US ADR, since Finnhub's free tier doesn't reliably cover the LSE listing); this placeholder is only shown if that's unavailable/empty. A 12-month price target is NOT available free anywhere we found — check a broker or financial news site yourself and record the source + date if you add one.
